Hi Ethan —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep procurement moving: 

- Current preference you mentioned: ScoutEdge will aim to use a Purchase Order (PO) for production contracts; pilot may run on a corporate card.
- Procurement constraints: AP requires vendor registration + W9 and will only issue a PO once vendor onboarding is complete (you estimated ~4–6 weeks).
- Marketplace approach: you said internal buying team is evaluating cloud marketplace options but no decision yet.

What we can do from our side:
- Share a vendor onboarding packet (attached) for your AP team to start supplier registration.
- Redwood Finance can accept PO-based billing with Net30 for contracted scopes; for short pilots we can accept card payments to get started faster.
- I’ll loop in our procurement lead to prep the standard SOW and provide a sample invoice layout that matches how ScoutEdge needs POs/line items.

Requested next steps:
1) Can you share the ScoutEdge procurement contact (name + email) and any internal form or portal link they use?
2) Confirm whether a one-off vendor request form or a full vendor packet is required up front.
3) If PO is the path, please provide target date range when your AP can issue a PO after packet submission.

I attached the Redwood_Vendor_Onboarding_Packet.pdf and a short AP checklist. Happy to join a quick 20-min sync with your procurement team next week — tell me what works.

Thanks,

Hi Marissa —

Appreciate the summary. Quick answers from AP side (copied Vanessa who owns vendor onboarding):

- We do prefer PO for any production agreements. Pilots historically go on card but AP will flag any spend above $10k for PO.
- Vendor registration: full packet required (W9, ACH details, vendor questionnaire). When we get the packet submitted and validated, AP can issue a PO — historically that’s ~30–45 business days depending on tax review.
- Marketplace: we’re in the early stages evaluating a marketplace for third-party tools; procurement wants the vendor listed there for longer-term procurement automation, but that won’t block the PO path.

I attached our AP matrix that summarizes what triggers a PO vs card for different teams. Vanessa — can you confirm the earliest dates AP could kick off once we receive the packet?

Best,

Hi Marissa —

Confirming what Ethan said. If you can submit the vendor packet this week we can start the validation process immediately. Our rough timing:

- Day 0: packet received -> initial intake
- Day 3–7: AP validation + W9/ACH check
- Day 10–20: tax/finance review (depends on workload)
